maria: FYI reproducible edge-case in sample-app fncall flow. When auth retry triggers the SDK sometimes sends function_call.arguments as a string (double-serialized).
alan: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal example/log?
maria: Minimal repro (python SDK): after a 401/retry we observe outgoing body like:
```json
{
  "function_call": {
    "name": "create_event",
    "arguments": "{\"title\":\"Lunch\",\"time\":\"12:30\"}"
  }
}
```
Note arguments is a JSON string, not an object.
sam: Is this just py or same in js? :thinking:
maria: Only hit in Python so far. JS returns arguments as an object.
jen: My hunch: retry middleware re-serializes request body when it replays the request, and json-mode helper already serialized it once. Double-dump.
alan: We had a similar layering bug in an HTTP middleware earlier. Add a unit test simulating 401 and assert outgoing function_call.arguments type.
dev-bot: CI: sample-app/fncall tests failing (3 tests) in run 2025-11-02T08:12:01Z
maria: Workaround for users: patch retry hook to skip encoding if body is str/bytes, but that's fragile.
sam: I'll take it. Plan: add integration test that forces token refresh on first try, assert outgoing body keeps arguments as object. Also make serializer idempotent.
jen: Also add a tiny e2e example to bootcamp so new users don't hit this while onboarding.
alan: And add an SDK-parity test between JS and Py for fncall/jsonmode to assert types match.
maria: PR opened with failing test + proposed fix (check type before dumping): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234
sam: Instead of sprinkling type-checks, consider centralizing serialization in transport and have retry operate on serialized blob. That should avoid per-sdk differences.
jen: Agree. Also update structured-output docs to clarify how function_call.arguments are represented in JSON mode vs raw mode.
alan: Add a migration note for customers who implemented custom retry middleware.
maria: Thanks team, will follow up in PR with CI logs. If anyone sees this in JS, flag it; current repro is py-only. :eyes: :bug:
